execution_overview.overall_summary: Executed both tasks in Python inside Docker. Implemented Poisson GLMs with HC0 robust SEs and a Negative Binomial model (Task1). Fixed code issues related to robust covariance, pandas chained assignment, and confidence interval indexing. Outputs show a positive association between first_A and overall complaints. With all controls, the Poisson model yields a marginal p-value (~0.055), while simpler Poisson models show strong positive significance. The NB model exhibited convergence issues and produced unreliable uncertainty estimates.

deviations.description: Adjusted statsmodels robust covariance usage by fitting GLM with cov_type='HC0' and updated CI extraction to handle pandas objects robustly.
deviations.reason: Original code used get_robustcov_results (not available in the installed statsmodels) and assumed numpy arrays for conf_int.

deviations.description: Replaced pandas chained assignment with non-inplace assignment for log_emp_size replace.
deviations.reason: Avoid ChainedAssignmentError under pandas Copy-on-Write semantics.

deviations.description: Hardened Negative Binomial result summarization to tolerate convergence issues and missing bse/cov.
deviations.reason: NB model had convergence/Hessian inversion warnings leading to missing SE/CI; ensured JSON output still writes.

method_fidelity.fidelity_note: Followed the planned Poisson and Negative Binomial specifications with the stated predictors and robust SEs; only technical repairs were made.

other.model: Poisson GLM with all controls and HC0 robust SEs

result_raw.result_text: In the fully controlled Poisson model, first_A is positively associated with more complaints (IRR≈1.54) with a marginal p-value (~0.055).

conclusion.conclusion_text: Evidence is mixed: simpler Poisson models strongly support a positive first_A effect, but with all controls the effect is only marginal (p≈0.055). NB model did not provide reliable uncertainty due to convergence issues.
